question: A sorted list of 19 numbers (smallest first) is searched for 23. The positions are numbered 1 to 19. The search keeps a lower position (first 1) and an upper position (first 19). Each round it looks at the number in the position halfway between them, rounded down when needed (the sum of the two positions divided by 2, rounded down). If that number is the target the search stops; if the target is smaller, the upper position becomes one less than the position just looked at; otherwise the lower position becomes one more. If the lower position ever exceeds the upper position the search stops, having found nothing. The list: 8, 9, 15, 19, 21, 23, 24, 27, 35, 39, 44, 49, 59, 61, 62, 65, 69, 72, 75. What is the sum of all the numbers the search looks at (a number looked at twice would count twice)?

A heap is a row of numbers in positions 1, 2, 3, ... where the number in position p is never larger than the numbers in positions 2p and 2p+1 (when those exist). To remove the smallest: take out the number in position 1, put the number from the last position into position 1 (the row is now one shorter), then, while it is larger than the smaller of the numbers in positions 2p and 2p+1 (those that exist), swap it with that smaller number.
